newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-HUNGARY SECONDARY BOND YIELDS SEEN STABLE.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-HUNGARY SECONDARY BOND YIELDS SEEN STABLE.

text.p: The central bank's reduction of most of its repo rates on Monday is unlikely to affect secondary market bond yield curves this week unless players take the cut as a sign of increased anti-inflation struggle, dealers said.
The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said earlier on Monday that it cut its overnight repo, one-week repo, one-week reverse repo and one-month reverse repo rates by 0.5 percentage points each.
"Falling interest rates have already been built into the two-year and three-year bond yields, so the repo cut is not likely to have much of an effect," Gabor Szogi of Creditanstalt Securities.
Bonds trade significantly below short-term treasury bills in the Hungarian market.
He added that yields on the three-year bonds are likely to stay around 17.5 and 17.7 percent in relatively passive trading this week.
He added, however, that if the NBH cuts its six-month depo rates, that could have an effect on bonds, especially the shorter maturities.
Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta said, however, that the market might take the NBH's 0.5 percent repo cut as a sign that monetary authorities are getting tougher on inflation.

"The NBH has not cut repo rates by 0.5 percent since last March (when inter-bank interest rates were falling rapidly)," he said. "This is not a reaction to the market('s expectation of lower interest rates) but a message that interest rates and inflation should fall at a faster pace."
Hungary plans to reduce inflation to 17 to 19 percent in 1997 from 23.6 percent last year, and to cut it by at least further five percentage points in 1998.

Finance Ministry officials, urged by the IMF for a radical cut, said recently that the 1998 budget draft, already being prepared, may include a reduction larger than five percentage points and may even target single-figure inflation.
